- NULL for active records
- Set to current timestamp when record is soft deleted
- Queries should filter out records where deleted_at IS NOT NULL

models.name: todo_app_member_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens for member registration and email change validation.

This table stores temporary verification tokens used during the member registration process and when members change their email address. Each token is associated with a specific member account and email address, and expires after a configured time period.

## Token Lifecycle

- Tokens are created when a member registers or requests an email change
- Tokens must be verified within their expiration window
- Once verified, the verified_at timestamp is set and the token becomes invalid
- Expired tokens are cleaned up periodically

## Security Considerations

- Tokens are single-use and expire automatically
- Each token is uniquely identified and linked to a specific member
- The email field captures the target email address for verification

## Relationship to {@link todo_app_members}

Each verification record belongs to exactly one member account. A member may have multiple pending verifications (e.g., during registration or email change workflows).

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Unique identifier for this email verification record.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_member_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the member account requiring email verification.

This foreign key links the verification record to the member who initiated the verification process. The member may be in a partially registered state (pending email confirmation) or may be an existing member requesting an email address change.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description:
Email address being verified.

This is the target email address that the member is attempting to verify. During registration, this is the email provided during sign-up. During an email change, this is the new email address being validated.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description:
Random verification token.

A cryptographically secure random string used to validate the verification request. This token is sent to the email address and must be presented back to the system to complete verification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this verification record was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this verification token expires.

Tokens are invalidated after this time to prevent replay attacks and ensure time-limited verification windows.

plainFields.name: verified_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when verification was completed.

This field is null until the token is successfully verified. Once set, the token is considered used and cannot be reused.

models.name: todo_app_todos
models.description:
Main todo task entity storing user's task items with title, description, dates, and completion status for personal task management.

**Core Attributes**

Each todo represents a task that a member can create, track, and manage. Todos support optional start and due dates for scheduling, and maintain completion status for workflow tracking.

**Lifecycle Management**

Todos support soft deletion through the deleted_at field, allowing users to recover accidentally deleted tasks. Permanently deleted todos (from trash) are removed from the database along with their snapshots.

**Ownership and Privacy**

Each todo belongs to exactly one {@link todo_app_members} account. Users can only access their own todos through proper authentication and authorization checks. No sharing or cross-user visibility is supported.

**Edit History**

Every modification to a todo creates a corresponding snapshot in {@link todo_app_snapshots}, enabling users to view the complete edit history of their tasks.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Unique identifier for this todo task.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_member_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the member who owns this todo task.

Each todo belongs to exactly one member account. This foreign key establishes the ownership relationship and enables filtering todos by user.

**Access Control**

Queries must always filter by this field to ensure users can only access their own todos. Authorization middleware validates that the authenticated member matches this foreign key before allowing any operations.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description:
The main title or name of the todo task.

This is a required field that provides a brief, descriptive name for the task. The title appears in todo lists and is the primary identifier users see when browsing their tasks.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
Detailed description or notes for the todo task.

This optional field contains additional context, instructions, or notes related to the task. It can be left empty if no additional details are needed.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description:
Optional planned start date for the todo task.

When set, this indicates when the user plans to begin working on the task. It is used for scheduling and filtering tasks by date range.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description:
Optional due date or deadline for the todo task.

When set, this indicates when the task should be completed. It is used for scheduling, reminders, and filtering tasks by deadline.

plainFields.name: is_completed
plainFields.description:
Completion status of the todo task.

Defaults to false when the todo is created. Users can toggle this field to mark the task as complete or incomplete. Completed tasks remain in the list but are visually distinguished from active tasks.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this todo was originally created.

This field is automatically set when the todo is first created and cannot be modified. It is used for sorting todos by creation order and tracking task age.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this todo was last modified.

This field is automatically updated whenever any field of the todo is changed. It is used for detecting concurrent modifications and sorting by recency.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this todo was soft deleted.

When this field is null, the todo is active and appears in normal todo lists. When set to a datetime value, the todo is considered deleted and hidden from regular lists (moved to trash). Permanently deleting a todo removes this record entirely from the database.

models.name: todo_app_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of todos capturing full state whenever edits occur, enabling users to view complete edit history.

Each snapshot records the complete state of a todo at the moment it was edited, including title, description, dates, and completion status. This allows users to browse the full edit history of their todos in chronological order.

Relationships

Each snapshot belongs to exactly one {@link todo_app_todos} record. When a todo is permanently deleted from the trash, all its associated snapshots are cascade deleted.

Data Retention

Snapshots are immutable once created. They accumulate as users edit their todos and are only removed when the parent todo is permanently deleted.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Unique identifier for each snapshot entry.

foreignFields.name: todo_app_todos_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the todo this snapshot belongs to.

Each snapshot is associated with exactly one todo record. When the todo is permanently deleted, all its snapshots are cascade deleted.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Title of the todo at the time this snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Description of the todo at the time this snapshot was created. May be empty if no description was set.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description: Start date of the todo at the time this snapshot was created. Null if no start date was set.

plainFields.name: due_date
plainFields.description: Due date of the todo at the time this snapshot was created. Null if no due date was set.

plainFields.name: is_completed
plainFields.description: Completion status of the todo at the time this snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this snapshot was created, representing the exact moment of the todo edit.

### `todo_app_guests`

Temporary guest accounts identified by device fingerprint for anonymous
access tracking.

Guest accounts enable anonymous users to interact with limited public
features without registration. Each guest is uniquely identified by their
device fingerprint, allowing session continuity across requests from the
same device.

**Identity and Tracking**

The device_fingerprint field serves as the primary identifier for guest
users. This enables the system to track anonymous activity and maintain
session state without requiring email or password credentials. Guests
have no access to protected resources and cannot view other users' data.

**Lifecycle Management**

Guest accounts follow a soft delete pattern via the deleted_at field.
When a guest account is deleted, it is marked as deleted but not
permanently removed from the database. This supports audit trails and
potential recovery scenarios. The updated_at field tracks when the
account was last modified.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key uniquely identifying each guest account.
- `device_fingerprint`
  > Unique device fingerprint identifying the guest user's device.
  >
  > This field serves as the primary identifier for anonymous guests. It
  > enables the system to associate multiple sessions and requests with the
  > same guest user without requiring authentication credentials.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the guest account was created.
  >
  > This field is automatically set upon guest account creation and cannot be
  > modified. It is used for tracking account age and for temporal queries.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the guest account was last updated.
  >
  > This field is automatically updated whenever the guest account record is
  > modified. It is used for tracking recent activity and for synchronization
  > purposes.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the guest account was soft deleted.
  >
  > When this field is null, the account is active. When populated, the
  > account is marked as deleted but retained in the database for audit
  > purposes. Soft deletion allows for potential recovery and maintains
  > referential integrity with related records.

### `todo_app_guest_sessions`

Temporary session tokens for guest access with device-based identification.

This table tracks active session tokens for guest users who access the
system without registration. Each session is associated with a {@link
todo_app_guest} and stores connection metadata for audit purposes.

**Session Lifecycle**
Sessions are created when a guest first accesses the system and expire
based on the expired_at timestamp. Expired sessions should be cleaned up
periodically to maintain database performance.

**Security Considerations**
Sessions are append-only and managed exclusively through authentication
flows. Users cannot directly modify or delete session records.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key uniquely identifying this session record.
- `todo_app_guest_id`
  > Reference to the guest account this session belongs to.
  >
  > Each session is associated with exactly one [todo_app_guest](#todo_app_guest)
  > identified by device fingerprint. This foreign key establishes the
  > ownership relationship and enables session cleanup when guests are
  > removed.
- `ip`
  > Client IP address from the session creation request.
  >
  > Used for security auditing and detecting suspicious access patterns.
  > Stored as string to accommodate both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
- `href`
  > Current page URL (window.location.href) when session was created.
  >
  > Provides context about where the user originated from within the
  > application.
- `referrer`
  > Referrer URL from the HTTP request headers.
  >
  > Indicates the external page or source that led the user to this
  > application.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this session was created.
  >
  > Used for session ordering, expiration calculations, and audit trails.
  > Automatically set on insertion.
- `expired_at`
  > Timestamp when this session expires and becomes invalid.
  >
  > Sessions past this timestamp should be rejected by authentication
  > middleware. Set to a future date at creation based on session timeout
  > policy.

### `todo_app_members`

Registered member accounts with email/password credentials and display
name profile.

This table represents authenticated users who can manage their own todos
and profile information. Each member has a unique email address used for
login authentication and a display name shown in the user interface.

**Authentication**

Members authenticate using email and password. The password_hash field
stores the securely hashed password, never plaintext. Email must be
unique across all accounts to ensure proper authentication routing.

**Profile**

The display_name field contains the user's chosen public name shown in
the application. Members can update their display name independently of
their authentication credentials.

**Lifecycle**

Soft delete support via deleted_at enables account recovery and audit
compliance. When a member deletes their account, all associated data
(todos, sessions, password resets, email verifications) is permanently
removed through cascade deletes.

**Relationships**

This is a parent table referenced by child tables: {@link
todo_app_member_sessions}, [todo_app_member_password_resets](#todo_app_member_password_resets),
[todo_app_member_email_verifications](#todo_app_member_email_verifications). Foreign keys flow from
children to this table, never the reverse.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key uniquely identifying each member account.
- `email`
  > Unique email address used for login authentication.
  >
  > This field serves as the primary identifier for member authentication. It
  > must be unique across all accounts and is validated during registration
  > and login flows.
- `password_hash`
  > Securely hashed password for authentication.
  >
  > Stores the bcrypt or Argon2 hash of the user's password. Never store
  > plaintext passwords. This field is updated when the member changes their
  > password.
- `display_name`
  > User's chosen display name shown in the application.
  >
  > This is the public name associated with the member's account. Members can
  > update their display name independently through profile management
  > operations.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when the member account was created.
  >
  > Records the initial account creation time for audit and compliance
  > purposes.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the member account was last modified.
  >
  > Updated whenever any field changes (email, password_hash, display_name).
  > Used for conflict detection and audit trails.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when the member account was soft-deleted.
  >
  > Null for active accounts. When set, the account is logically deleted but
  > retained for recovery purposes. All associated data cascades to permanent
  > deletion.

### `todo_app_member_sessions`

JWT session tokens with access and refresh token support for member
authentication.

This table tracks active login sessions for authenticated members,
storing JWT tokens and session metadata for security and audit purposes.

## Session Lifecycle

Sessions are created during member login and expire based on token
expiration times. Members can have multiple active sessions across
different devices or browsers.

## Security Considerations

Each session tracks the originating IP address, href, and referrer for
security auditing. Expired sessions should be cleaned up periodically to
maintain database performance.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary key uniquely identifying this session record.
- `todo_app_member_id`
  > References the member account that owns this session.

  > This foreign key establishes the relationship between the session and its
  > parent [todo_app_members](#todo_app_members) actor. Each session belongs to exactly
  > one member, and a member can have multiple active sessions.
  >
  > ## Relationship Semantics
  >
  > - **Cardinality**: Many sessions belong to one member (1:N)
  > - **Ownership**: Sessions are owned by and cannot exist without their
  > parent member
  > - **Cascade**: When a member account is deleted, all their sessions are
  > automatically removed

  > It contains encoded claims about the user identity and permissions, and
  > has a relatively short expiration time for security.
- `refresh_token`
  > JWT refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.
  >
  > This long-lived token allows members to obtain new access tokens without
  > re-authenticating. It is used when the access token expires, enabling
  > seamless user experience while maintaining security through token
  > rotation.
- `ip`
  > IP address of the client that created this session.
  >
  > Captured at session creation time for security auditing and anomaly
  > detection. Helps identify potentially unauthorized access attempts from
  > unusual locations.
- `href`
  > The URL (href) of the page where the login occurred.
  >
  > Tracks the origin page for security auditing and user experience
  > analytics. Can help identify suspicious login patterns or phishing
  > attempts.
- `referrer`
  > The referrer URL that led to the login page.
  >
  > Captures the referring page for security auditing and analytics. Useful
  > for understanding user acquisition paths and detecting suspicious
  > referral patterns.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this session was created.
  >
  > Records the exact moment the member logged in and this session was
  > established. Used for session ordering, expiration calculations, and
  > audit trails.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this session was last updated.
  >
  > Tracks the most recent modification to this session record. Updated
  > whenever session metadata changes or tokens are refreshed.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when this session was soft-deleted.
  >
  > Used for soft delete functionality, allowing sessions to be marked as
  > deleted without immediate physical removal. Enables session recovery and
  > audit trail preservation.
- `expired_at`
  > Timestamp when this session expires.
  >
  > Defines the absolute expiration time for this session. Sessions past this
  > timestamp should be considered invalid and cleaned up. Typically set
  > based on refresh token expiration policy.

### `todo_app_member_password_resets`

Password reset tokens with expiration for member password recovery workflow.

This table stores one-time use tokens that allow members to securely
reset their passwords without knowing their current password. Each token
is linked to a specific member account and expires after a configured
time period.

**Token Lifecycle**

Tokens are generated when a member requests a password reset via email.
The token is sent to the member's registered email address and must be
used within the expiration window. Once used, the token is marked as
consumed and cannot be reused.

**Security Considerations**

Tokens are cryptographically random strings that cannot be guessed.
Expired or used tokens are automatically invalidated. Old tokens are
cleaned up periodically to prevent database bloat.

**Relationships**

Each reset token belongs to exactly one [todo_app_members](#todo_app_members) account.
Multiple tokens may exist for the same member if they request multiple
resets, but only the most recent active token is typically valid.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Unique identifier for this password reset token record.
- `todo_app_member_id`
  > Reference to the member account requesting password reset.
  >
  > This foreign key links the reset token to the specific member whose
  > password will be reset. The member must exist in the {@link
  > todo_app_members} table.
  >
  > **Relationship Semantics**
  >
  > - A member can have multiple reset tokens over time (historical records)
  > - When a member is deleted, their reset tokens should be cascade deleted
  > - This is a many-to-one relationship: many tokens can reference one member
- `token`
  > Cryptographically random reset token string.
  >
  > This is the actual token value that is sent to the member via email. It
  > must be unique across all reset tokens and is what the member provides
  > when completing the password reset flow.
  >
  > **Security Requirements**
  >
  > - Must be generated using a cryptographically secure random number
  > generator
  > - Should be at least 32 characters of alphanumeric or base64-encoded data
  > - Must never be logged or stored in plaintext in application logs
- `expires_at`
  > Timestamp when this token becomes invalid.
  >
  > Tokens expire after a configured duration (typically 1 hour) to limit the
  > window for potential abuse. The password reset flow validates that the
  > current time is before this timestamp.
  >
  > **Validation Logic**
  >
  > - Password reset requests check: current_time < expires_at
  > - Expired tokens are rejected even if not yet used
  > - This field is NOT NULL to ensure all tokens have a defined expiration
- `used_at`
  > Timestamp when this token was consumed for password reset.
  >
  > Once a token is used to reset a password, this field is populated with
  > the timestamp. Used tokens cannot be reused for additional password
  > resets.
  >
  > **Usage Flow**
  >
  > - Initially NULL when token is created
  > - Set to current timestamp when password reset is completed
  > - Used tokens are logically deleted from active rotation
  > - Nullable to support both unused (NULL) and used (timestamp) states
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this password reset token was created.
  >
  > Records the exact moment the token was generated and sent to the member.
  > Used for auditing and cleanup of expired tokens.
  >
  > **Temporal Tracking**
  >
  > - Always set to current timestamp on insert
  > - Never updated after creation
  > - Required for all records
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this record was last modified.
  >
  > Updated when the token is used (used_at field is set). Provides audit

  >
  > **Update Behavior**
  >
  > - Set on token creation
  > - Updated when token is consumed (used_at is populated)
  > - Never updated for other modifications
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when this record was soft deleted.
  >
  > Used for soft delete support, allowing token records to be retained for
  > audit purposes while being logically removed from active queries.
  >
  > **Soft Delete Behavior**
  >
  > - NULL for active records
  > - Set to current timestamp when record is soft deleted
  > - Queries should filter out records where deleted_at IS NOT NULL

### `todo_app_member_email_verifications`

validation.

This table stores temporary verification tokens used during the member

### `todo_app_todos`

Main todo task entity storing user's task items with title, description,
dates, and completion status for personal task management.

**Core Attributes**

Each todo represents a task that a member can create, track, and manage.
Todos support optional start and due dates for scheduling, and maintain
completion status for workflow tracking.

**Lifecycle Management**

Todos support soft deletion through the deleted_at field, allowing users
to recover accidentally deleted tasks. Permanently deleted todos (from
trash) are removed from the database along with their snapshots.

**Ownership and Privacy**

Each todo belongs to exactly one [todo_app_members](#todo_app_members) account. Users
can only access their own todos through proper authentication and
authorization checks. No sharing or cross-user visibility is supported.

**Edit History**

Every modification to a todo creates a corresponding snapshot in {@link
todo_app_snapshots}, enabling users to view the complete edit history of
their tasks.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Unique identifier for this todo task.
- `todo_app_member_id`
  > Reference to the member who owns this todo task.
  >
  > Each todo belongs to exactly one member account. This foreign key
  > establishes the ownership relationship and enables filtering todos by
  > user.
  >
  > **Access Control**
  >
  > Queries must always filter by this field to ensure users can only access
  > their own todos. Authorization middleware validates that the
  > authenticated member matches this foreign key before allowing any
  > operations.
- `title`
  > The main title or name of the todo task.
  >
  > This is a required field that provides a brief, descriptive name for the
  > task. The title appears in todo lists and is the primary identifier users
  > see when browsing their tasks.
- `description`
  > Detailed description or notes for the todo task.
  >
  > This optional field contains additional context, instructions, or notes
  > related to the task. It can be left empty if no additional details are
  > needed.
- `start_date`
  > Optional planned start date for the todo task.
  >
  > When set, this indicates when the user plans to begin working on the
  > task. It is used for scheduling and filtering tasks by date range.
- `due_date`
  > Optional due date or deadline for the todo task.
  >
  > When set, this indicates when the task should be completed. It is used
  > for scheduling, reminders, and filtering tasks by deadline.
- `is_completed`
  > Completion status of the todo task.
  >
  > Defaults to false when the todo is created. Users can toggle this field
  > to mark the task as complete or incomplete. Completed tasks remain in the
  > list but are visually distinguished from active tasks.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this todo was originally created.
  >
  > This field is automatically set when the todo is first created and cannot
  > be modified. It is used for sorting todos by creation order and tracking
  > task age.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when this todo was last modified.
  >
  > This field is automatically updated whenever any field of the todo is
  > changed. It is used for detecting concurrent modifications and sorting by
  > recency.
- `deleted_at`
  > Timestamp when this todo was soft deleted.
  >
  > When this field is null, the todo is active and appears in normal todo
  > lists. When set to a datetime value, the todo is considered deleted and
  > hidden from regular lists (moved to trash). Permanently deleting a todo
  > removes this record entirely from the database.

### `todo_app_snapshots`

Point-in-time snapshots of todos capturing full state whenever edits
occur, enabling users to view complete edit history.

Each snapshot records the complete state of a todo at the moment it was
edited, including title, description, dates, and completion status. This
allows users to browse the full edit history of their todos in
chronological order.

Relationships

Each snapshot belongs to exactly one [todo_app_todos](#todo_app_todos) record. When
a todo is permanently deleted from the trash, all its associated
snapshots are cascade deleted.

Data Retention

Snapshots are immutable once created. They accumulate as users edit their
todos and are only removed when the parent todo is permanently deleted.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Unique identifier for each snapshot entry.
- `todo_app_todos_id`
  > Reference to the todo this snapshot belongs to.
  >
  > Each snapshot is associated with exactly one todo record. When the todo
  > is permanently deleted, all its snapshots are cascade deleted.
- `title`: Title of the todo at the time this snapshot was created.
- `description`
  > Description of the todo at the time this snapshot was created. May be
  > empty if no description was set.
- `start_date`
  > Start date of the todo at the time this snapshot was created. Null if no
  > start date was set.
- `due_date`
  > Due date of the todo at the time this snapshot was created. Null if no
  > due date was set.
- `is_completed`: Completion status of the todo at the time this snapshot was created.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp when this snapshot was created, representing the exact moment
  > of the todo edit.

instruction:
User Account APIs:
- POST /auth/signup: Register new user with email and password
- POST /auth/login: Log in user with email and password
- PUT /auth/password: Change user's password (requires current password)
- DELETE /auth/account: Delete user account (permanently deletes all todos and history)

User Profile APIs:
- GET /profile: Get current user's profile (display name)
- PUT /profile: Update current user's display name

Todo APIs:
- POST /todos: Create a new todo with title (required), description (optional), start date (optional), due date (optional)
- GET /todos: List user's todos with pagination, filtering, and sorting
  - Query params: page, limit, status (all/complete/incomplete), sortBy (createdAt/startDate/dueDate), sortOrder (asc/desc)
- GET /todos/:id: Get a single todo's full details including description
- PUT /todos/:id: Update todo's title, description, start date, and/or due date
- PATCH /todos/:id/complete: Toggle todo completion status (complete/incomplete)
- DELETE /todos/:id: Soft delete a todo (moves to trash)

Todo History APIs:
- GET /todos/:id/history: Get edit history for a specific todo (sorted most recent to oldest)

Trash APIs:
- GET /trash: List user's deleted todos with pagination
  - Query params: page, limit
- PUT /trash/:id/restore: Restore a deleted todo from trash
- DELETE /trash/:id: Permanently delete a todo from trash (also deletes its edit history)

Privacy Requirements:
- All endpoints require authentication
- Users can only access their own todos, history, and trash
- No endpoints exist to access other users' data

operations.description:
Register a new guest user or retrieve existing guest by device fingerprint.

This endpoint creates a guest account when a new device accesses the system, or returns the existing guest identity if the device has registered before. Guest accounts are identified solely by device fingerprint, requiring no email or password credentials.

**Business Logic**
- Accept device_fingerprint from request body
- Search for existing guest with matching fingerprint
- If found and not soft-deleted: return existing guest's session
- If not found or soft-deleted: create new guest record and session
- Generate JWT access token for the guest session

**Schema Integration**
- Creates record in todo_app_guests with device_fingerprint
- Creates associated todo_app_guest_sessions record
- Sets created_at and updated_at timestamps
- Session expires_at set based on configured timeout

**Error Handling**
- Return 400 if device_fingerprint is missing or empty
- Return 500 on database errors during guest or session creation

responseBody.description: Guest authorization tokens and session information

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Refresh an existing guest session token. Validate the provided session token is valid and not expired. Look up the guest session by token, verify expired_at is in the future, then generate a new access token with extended expiration. Update the session's expired_at timestamp in todo_app_guest_sessions table. Return new authorized response with refreshed tokens. Return 401 if session is expired or invalid.
operations.description:
Refresh the session token for an existing guest user.

This endpoint extends the session lifetime for authenticated guest users by generating a new access token. It validates the current session token and updates its expiration timestamp.

**Business Logic**
- Accept current session token in request body
- Validate token signature and extract guest session ID
- Look up session in todo_app_guest_sessions table
- Verify session has not expired (expired_at > now)
- Generate new access token with extended expiration
- Update session's expired_at timestamp
- Return new authorized response with refreshed tokens

**Schema Integration**
- Reads from todo_app_guest_sessions by session ID
- Updates expired_at timestamp on session record
- Links to todo_app_guests for guest identity verification

**Security Considerations**
- Token validation prevents unauthorized refresh attempts
- Expired sessions are rejected with 401 response
- Session expiration configured per application policy

**Error Handling**
- Return 401 if session token is invalid or expired
- Return 401 if associated guest account is soft-deleted
- Return 500 on database errors during session lookup or update

responseBody.description: Refreshed guest authorization tokens and session information

operations.description:
Register a new member account with email and password credentials.

This endpoint creates a new authenticated user account in the system. Upon successful registration, the member account is created with the provided email and password, and an email verification token is generated for account validation.

**Registration Process**

The service validates the email format and checks for uniqueness in the todo_app_members table. If the email is available, the password is securely hashed and the member record is created. An email verification token is generated in the todo_app_member_email_verifications table to validate ownership of the email address.

**Schema Fields Used**

- email: Unique identifier for authentication (todo_app_members.email)
- password: Securely stored as password_hash (todo_app_members.password_hash)
- display_name: Optional public name (todo_app_members.display_name, defaults to email prefix)

**Error Handling**

Returns 409 Conflict if the email is already registered, 400 Bad Request for invalid email format or weak password, and 500 Internal Server Error for database failures.

requestBody.description: Registration credentials for new member account creation

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and member identification after successful registration

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Authenticate a member with email and password. The service must: 1) Look up the member by email in todo_app_members table, 2) Verify the password_hash matches the provided password using bcrypt/Argon2 comparison, 3) Generate JWT access_token and refresh_token, 4) Create a session record in todo_app_member_sessions with tokens, IP, href, and referrer, 5) Return 401 Unauthorized if email not found or password mismatch, 400 for invalid input format. The session's expired_at should be set based on refresh token expiration policy.
operations.description:
Authenticate a member with email and password credentials.

This endpoint validates member credentials and establishes an authenticated session by generating JWT tokens. Upon successful authentication, access and refresh tokens are returned along with session information.

**Authentication Process**

The service retrieves the member record by email from the todo_app_members table and validates the password against the stored password_hash. If credentials are valid, JWT access and refresh tokens are generated and a session record is created in todo_app_member_sessions with client metadata (IP address, href, referrer) for security auditing.

**Schema Fields Used**

- email: Authentication identifier (todo_app_members.email)
- password: Validated against password_hash (todo_app_members.password_hash)
- display_name: Included in token claims for user identification

**Session Management**

Each login creates a new session record tracking the access_token, refresh_token, and client information. Multiple sessions can exist for the same member across different devices. Sessions expire based on the expired_at timestamp.

**Error Handling**

Returns 401 Unauthorized for invalid email or password, 400 Bad Request for malformed input, and 500 Internal Server Error for authentication service failures.

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and member identification after successful login

operations.specification: Renew authentication tokens using a valid refresh token. The service must: 1) Validate the refresh_token exists in todo_app_member_sessions and is not expired, 2) Verify the session's expired_at is in the future, 3) Generate new access_token and optionally rotate refresh_token, 4) Update the session record with new tokens and updated_at timestamp, 5) Return 401 Unauthorized if refresh token is invalid, expired, or already used, 400 for missing refresh_token. Implement token rotation by invalidating the old refresh_token and creating a new one.
operations.description:
Renew authentication tokens using a valid refresh token.

This endpoint extends the authenticated session by generating new access and refresh tokens without requiring re-authentication. It enables seamless user experience while maintaining security through token rotation.

**Token Renewal Process**

The service validates the provided refresh_token against the todo_app_member_sessions table, checking that the session exists, is not expired, and the token has not been used. Upon validation, new JWT tokens are generated and the session record is updated with the new tokens and current timestamp.

**Schema Fields Used**

- refresh_token: Validated against stored refresh_token (todo_app_member_sessions.refresh_token)
- access_token: New access token generated and stored (todo_app_member_sessions.access_token)
- expired_at: Session expiration timestamp validated (todo_app_member_sessions.expired_at)
- updated_at: Updated to track token renewal (todo_app_member_sessions.updated_at)

**Security Considerations**

Token rotation is recommended: the old refresh_token is invalidated and a new one is issued. This limits the window of opportunity if a refresh token is compromised. Sessions are tracked by IP and referrer for anomaly detection.

**Error Handling**

Returns 401 Unauthorized for invalid, expired, or used refresh tokens, 400 Bad Request for missing refresh_token parameter, and 500 Internal Server Error for token generation failures.

operations.description:
Update the authenticated member's profile information.

This operation allows a logged-in member to update their display name. The member's email and password cannot be changed through this endpoint. All updates are validated against business rules before being persisted to the database.

**Updateable Fields**

- `displayName`: The user's chosen public name shown in the application interface

**Validation Rules**

- Display name is required and must not be empty
- Display name length must be between 1 and 100 characters

**Access Control**

- Requires valid authentication (member token)
- Only updates the authenticated member's own profile
- Returns 401 Unauthorized if not authenticated
- Returns 403 Forbidden if authentication is invalid
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Implement profile update for authenticated member.

**Authentication**
- Extract member ID from JWT token in Authorization header
- Validate token is not expired
- Return 401 if token missing or invalid

**Request Validation**
- Validate display_name is present if provided
- Validate display_name length (1-100 characters)
- Return 400 Bad Request with validation errors

**Database Update**
- Query: UPDATE todo_app_members SET display_name = $1, updated_at = $2 WHERE id = $3 AND deleted_at IS NULL
- Use member ID from authenticated token
- Return updated member record

**Error Handling**
- 401 Unauthorized: Missing or invalid authentication token
- 400 Bad Request: Validation errors on display_name
- 404 Not Found: Member not found or already deleted

**Response**
- Return 200 OK with updated member object
- Include updated_at timestamp

responseBody.description: Updated member profile object with current display name and metadata.

requestBody.description: Profile update request containing display name to update.

operations.description:
Retrieve a member's profile information by their unique identifier.

This endpoint returns the complete profile details for a specific member account, including their display name and email address. The authenticated member must match the requested memberId to ensure data privacy and isolation.

**Authorization**

Only the member themselves can access their own profile. Members cannot view or access another user's profile information. This enforces the private todo app's strict data isolation policy.

**Response Data**

The response includes the member's display name, email address, and account timestamps (created_at, updated_at). The password_hash is never exposed in API responses.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query todo_app_members table by UUID id parameter. Verify the authenticated member's ID matches the requested memberId in the path to enforce data isolation. Return 404 if member not found or if the member has been soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null). Return 403 if the authenticated member does not match the requested memberId. Include display_name, email, created_at, and updated_at in the response. Never expose password_hash field.

operations.description:
Update the current authenticated user's profile display name.

This operation allows members to modify their public display name that appears throughout the application. The display name is a user-defined identifier that represents them within the system.

**Access Control**

Only the authenticated user can update their own profile. Users cannot access or modify other users' profile information. The system enforces complete data isolation between users.

**Validation**

The display name must be provided and cannot be empty. The system validates the input before persisting changes to the database.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Verify the request has a valid authentication token (member session)
2. Extract the member_id from the authenticated session context
3. Validate the request body contains a non-empty display_name string
4. Query todo_app_members table: SELECT id, email, display_name, created_at, updated_at WHERE id = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL
5. If member not found or soft-deleted, return 404 Not Found
6. Update the record: UPDATE todo_app_members SET display_name = ?, updated_at = NOW() WHERE id = ?
7. Return the updated member record with id, email, display_name, created_at, updated_at
8. If authentication fails or session is invalid, return 401 Unauthorized
9. If validation fails (empty display_name), return 400 Bad Request

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of guest accounts with optional filtering and sorting.

This endpoint enables administrative search and browsing of guest user records tracked in the system. Guest accounts are identified by device fingerprint and represent unauthenticated visitors who have accessed the application.

**Filtering Capabilities**

Search criteria support filtering by device fingerprint patterns, creation date ranges, and deletion status. This allows administrators to locate specific guest sessions or analyze guest user patterns over time.

**Pagination**

Results are returned using cursor-based pagination to efficiently handle large datasets. Include page number and limit parameters to control result set size.

**Access Control**

This operation requires administrative authorization. Regular members and guests cannot access guest account information due to privacy and data isolation policies.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query the todo_app_guests table with pagination and filtering support.

**Implementation Steps**:
1. Validate admin authorization before proceeding
2. Build dynamic WHERE clause based on request filters:
   - device_fingerprint: LIKE pattern matching (case-insensitive)
   - created_at: date range filtering (gte, lte)
   - deleted_at: null check for active guests, not-null for deleted
3. Apply ORDER BY clause based on sortBy parameter (default: created_at DESC)
4. Implement cursor-based pagination using created_at as cursor field
5. Join with todo_app_guest_sessions if session statistics are requested
6. Return paginated response with IPageITodoAppGuest.ISummary type

**Edge Cases**:
- Empty result set: return empty items array with zero totals
- Invalid date formats: return 400 Bad Request
- Unauthorized access: return 403 Forbidden
- Soft-deleted guests: include based on deleted_at filter parameter

**Performance Considerations**:
- Use @@index([created_at) for efficient date range queries
- Consider composite index on (deleted_at, created_at) for filtered pagination
- Limit maximum page size to prevent excessive database load

Retrieve a paginated list of the authenticated member's active login sessions.

**Security and Privacy**

Only the authenticated member can view their own sessions. Session tokens (access_token, refresh_token) are excluded from the response for security. Each session record includes the originating IP address, page href, and referrer captured at login time for security auditing.

**Pagination and Filtering**

Supports cursor-based pagination for efficient browsing of session history. Filter by creation date range and sort by creation time or expiration time. Results are ordered newest-first by default.
operations.name: index

operations.description:
Consumes a password reset token to update a member's password.

This endpoint enables members to reset their password when they cannot provide their current password (e.g., forgotten password scenario). The system validates the reset token's existence, expiration status, and usage state before updating the password.

**Token Validation**

The provided reset token must exist in the system, not have expired (current time before expires_at), and not have been previously used (used_at is NULL). Invalid, expired, or consumed tokens are rejected.

**Password Requirements**

The new password must meet security requirements and be confirmed by entering it twice to prevent typographical errors. Upon successful validation, the member's password_hash is updated and the token is marked as consumed.

**Security Considerations**

This operation does not require authentication since the reset token itself serves as proof of identity. All password reset attempts are logged for security auditing.
operations.name: reset
operations.specification:
1. Receive request body with token, newPassword, and newPasswordConfirm fields.
2. Query todo_app_member_password_resets table to find the token record where token matches the provided value.
3. Validate the token record exists; return 404 if not found.
4. Check if used_at is NULL; return 400 if token has already been consumed.
5. Check if expires_at is in the future; return 400 if token has expired.
6. Validate newPassword and newPasswordConfirm match; return 400 if they differ.
7. Validate newPassword meets password policy requirements (minimum length, complexity).
8. Retrieve the associated todo_app_members record using todo_app_member_id foreign key.
9. Hash the new password using bcrypt or Argon2.
10. Update the member's password_hash field with the new hash.
11. Update the password reset token's used_at field to current timestamp.
12. Update both records' updated_at timestamps.
13. Return 200 success response.
14. Handle database transaction to ensure password update and token consumption are atomic.
15. Log password reset completion for security auditing.

responseBody.description: Password reset confirmation indicating successful password update.

requestBody.description: Password reset request containing the one-time reset token and new password with confirmation.

operations.description:
Validate a password reset token for the password recovery workflow.

This endpoint verifies that a password reset token exists, has not expired, and has not been used. It is called when a member clicks the password reset link in their email to confirm the token is valid before presenting the password reset form.

**Validation Rules**

- Token must exist in the database with deleted_at IS NULL
- Token must not be expired (current time < expires_at)
- Token must not have been used (used_at is NULL)

**Response Behavior**

Returns token metadata including expiration time and usage status. The actual token value is never returned in the response for security reasons. The client uses this information to determine if the password reset flow can proceed.

**Error Responses**

- 404: Token not found or has been soft deleted
- 410: Token has expired or has already been used
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the todo_app_member_password_resets table by id (UUID).

Implementation steps:
1. Fetch record WHERE id = {resetId} AND deleted_at IS NULL
2. If no record found, return 404 Not Found
3. Check expiration: if now() >= expires_at, return 410 Gone (token expired)
4. Check usage: if used_at IS NOT NULL, return 410 Gone (token already used)
5. Return token metadata object with:
   - expires_at: timestamp when token expires
   - used_at: null (since we already validated it's unused)
   - created_at: timestamp when token was created
   - valid: boolean true

Security considerations:
- NEVER return the token value in the response
- Use constant-time comparison for token validation to prevent timing attacks
- Log validation attempts for audit purposes
- Do not reveal whether a token exists vs. is invalid in error messages (use generic responses)

responseBody.description: Password reset token validation result containing token metadata and validity status. The actual token value is excluded for security purposes.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the password reset token in UUID format.
parameters.name: resetId

operations.description:
Submit an email verification token to confirm email ownership.

This endpoint validates a verification token sent to a member's email address during registration or email change workflows. When a valid token is submitted, the system marks the email verification as complete by setting the verified_at timestamp.

## Token Validation

The system validates the token against the following criteria:
- Token must exist in the email verifications table
- Token must not have expired (current time before expired_at)
- Token must not have been previously verified (verified_at is null)
- Token must match the authenticated member's pending verification

## Verification Outcome

Upon successful validation, the verified_at timestamp is set to the current time, making the token invalid for future use. The email address associated with the verification record is then considered confirmed.

## Error Handling

Invalid, expired, or already-used tokens return appropriate error responses without revealing which specific validation failed, preventing token enumeration attacks.
operations.name: verify
operations.specification:
Implement email verification token validation and confirmation.

## Implementation Steps

1. **Extract Token from Request Body**: Parse the verification token from the request payload.

2. **Identify Authenticated Member**: Retrieve the current member's ID from the session/authentication context.

3. **Query Verification Record**: Execute a database query on todo_app_member_email_verifications table:
   - Filter by token = provided token
   - Filter by todo_app_member_id = authenticated member ID
   - Filter by verified_at IS NULL (not yet verified)
   - Filter by expired_at > current timestamp (not expired)

4. **Validation Checks**:
   - If no record found, return 404 Not Found (do not distinguish between invalid token, expired, or already verified)
   - If record found, proceed to verification

5. **Mark as Verified**: Update the verification record:
   - Set verified_at = current timestamp
   - This makes the token single-use and prevents replay attacks

6. **Return Success Response**: Return 200 OK with verification confirmation.

## Security Considerations

- Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection
- Do not expose whether token was invalid, expired, or already used in error messages
- Ensure authenticated member can only verify their own pending verifications
- Token verification should be idempotent (multiple submissions of same valid token only succeed once)

## Database Transaction

Wrap the query and update in a transaction to ensure atomicity. If any step fails, roll back all changes.

## Edge Cases

- Token submitted after expiration: return error
- Token already verified: return error (idempotent behavior)
- Token belongs to different member: return 404 (do not reveal this distinction)
- Multiple pending verifications for same member: token uniquely identifies which one to verify

responseBody.description: Email verification confirmation result indicating successful token validation and email confirmation.

requestBody.description: Email verification token to be validated and confirmed.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single email verification record by its unique identifier.

This endpoint returns the complete details of an email verification token, including the associated member ID, email address, token status, and timestamps. It is used to check the verification status during registration or email change workflows.

## Verification Status

The response includes the `verifiedAt` field which is null if the token has not been verified yet. Once verified, this timestamp is set and the token becomes invalid for future verification attempts.

## Security and Access

Only authenticated members can access email verification records. Users can only retrieve their own verification records that are associated with their member account.

Return the full email verification entity including id, todoAppMemberId, email, token, createdAt, expiredAt, and verifiedAt fields. The verifiedAt field will be null for pending verifications and contain a timestamp for completed verifications.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of todos belonging to the authenticated user with optional filtering and sorting.

This operation supports comprehensive search capabilities including completion status filtering, date range queries, and customizable sorting. Users can browse their todo list efficiently with pagination controls.

**Filtering Options**

Filter todos by completion status (all, complete, incomplete), date ranges for start or due dates, and text search across title and description fields. Todos without dates appear at the end when sorting by date fields.

**Sorting**

Sort by creation time, start date, or due date in ascending or descending order. Null date values are placed at the end of sorted results.

**Pagination**

Results are paginated with configurable page size. The response includes pagination metadata for navigating through large result sets.

**Data Isolation**

Only todos belonging to the authenticated user are returned. Cross-user access is strictly prohibited.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query todo_app_todos table filtered by todo_app_member_id from authenticated session. Apply search filters from request body: completion status (is_completed), date ranges (start_date, due_date), and text search (title, description). Implement pagination with cursor or offset-based approach. Support sorting by createdAt, startDate, dueDate with ascending/descending order. Enforce data isolation by filtering WHERE todo_app_member_id = authenticated_user_id. Return paginated summary with total count and cursor/offset metadata. Handle null date fields by placing them at end of sorted results per requirements.

operations.description:
Retrieve a single todo's complete details by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the full todo entity including title, description, dates, and completion status. The authenticated user can only access todos that belong to them; attempts to access another user's todo will be denied.

**Access Control**

The system enforces strict data isolation. Users can only retrieve todos where the owner matches their authenticated account. Any request to access a todo belonging to another user will result in an authorization error.

**Response Content**

The response includes all todo attributes: title, optional description, optional start and due dates, completion status, and timestamps for creation and last modification.

Return 404 if todo not found or belongs to another user. Include all fields: id, title, description, start_date, due_date, is_completed, created_at, updated_at. Do not include deleted_at in response as this is for active todo retrieval.

operations.description:
Create a new todo task for the authenticated member.

This operation allows members to create task items with a required title and optional description, start date, and due date. The newly created todo is automatically marked as incomplete and associated with the authenticated member's account.

**Business Logic**

The system creates a todo record with the provided fields. The completion status defaults to incomplete. A snapshot is NOT created on initial creation—snapshots are only generated when the todo is subsequently edited. The todo is immediately visible in the member's active todo list.

**Security and Access Control**

Only authenticated members can create todos. The system automatically associates the new todo with the authenticated member's account. Members cannot create todos on behalf of other users.

**Relationships**

The created todo belongs to the authenticated member and can have multiple snapshots created when it is edited. These snapshots form the edit history that members can view later.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
1. Extract authenticated member ID from JWT session token.
2. Validate request body: title is required (min 1 character, max 255), description optional (max 1000), start_date and due_date optional DateTime values.
3. Validate date logic: if both start_date and due_date provided, due_date must be >= start_date.
4. Insert new todo_app_todos record with: todo_app_member_id (from auth), title, description, start_date, due_date, is_completed=false, deleted_at=null.
5. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp.
6. Return the created todo entity with all fields including generated id.
7. No snapshot is created on initial creation—only on subsequent edits.

responseBody.description: The newly created todo entity with all fields including the generated unique identifier, timestamps, and default completion status.

requestBody.description: Todo creation request containing title (required), and optional description, start date, and due date fields.

operations.description:
Update an existing todo's title, description, start date, and/or due date.

This operation allows authenticated members to modify their own todo tasks. When any field is updated, the system automatically creates a snapshot entry in the edit history for audit purposes.

**Updateable Fields**

- **title**: Required field that identifies the task
- **description**: Optional field for additional context (can be cleared)
- **start_date**: Optional planned start date (can be cleared)
- **due_date**: Optional deadline date (can be cleared)

**Access Control**

Only the todo's owner can update it. The system validates that the authenticated member matches the todo's owner before allowing modifications.

**Edit History**

Every update creates a new snapshot in the edit history, recording the timestamp and new values for all changed fields.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
1. Validate authentication - extract member ID from JWT token
2. Query todo_app_todos table by id (todoId path parameter)
3. Verify todo exists and todo_app_member_id matches authenticated member ID - return 404 if not found or 403 if ownership mismatch
4. Validate request body fields:
   - title: required, non-empty string
   - description: optional string (can be null or empty)
   - start_date: optional DateTime (can be null)
   - due_date: optional DateTime (can be null)
5. Begin database transaction
6. Update the todo record with provided fields
7. Set updated_at to current timestamp
8. Create a new snapshot in todo_app_snapshots table with:
   - todo_app_todos_id: the todo's ID
   - title, description, start_date, due_date, is_completed: current values
   - created_at: current timestamp
9. Commit transaction
10. Return the updated todo entity with 200 status

Edge cases:
- Todo not found: return 404
- Unauthorized access (wrong owner): return 403
- Invalid date format: return 400
- Concurrent modification (updated_at mismatch): return 409

responseBody.description: The fully updated todo entity including all fields and timestamps.

operations.description:
Soft delete a todo, moving it to the trash for potential recovery.

This operation performs a soft delete on the specified todo, setting its deleted_at timestamp. The todo is removed from the active list but remains accessible through the trash endpoint. Users can restore soft-deleted todos or permanently delete them from the trash.

**Access Control**: Only the todo owner can delete their own todos. The system validates that the authenticated member matches the todo's owner before allowing deletion.

**Error Handling**: Returns 404 if the todo does not exist or belongs to another user. Returns 400 if the todo is already deleted.

Check that deleted_at is null (todo is not already soft deleted). Update deleted_at to current timestamp. Return 204 No Content on success. Return 404 if todo not found or belongs to different user. Return 400 if todo is already soft deleted.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of soft-deleted todos from the user's trash.

This operation returns todos that have been deleted by the user but not yet permanently removed. Soft-deleted todos retain all their original attributes including title, description, dates, and completion status. Users can review deleted tasks and choose to restore them or permanently delete them.

## Access Control

Only the authenticated user's own deleted todos are returned. Users cannot access another user's trash.

## Pagination

Results are paginated to handle large numbers of deleted todos efficiently. Users can control the page number and page size through the request body parameters.

## Soft Delete Behavior

Todos in the trash are soft-deleted, meaning they remain in the database with a deleted_at timestamp set. They do not appear in the normal todo list but are accessible through this trash endpoint.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query todo_app_todos table filtering by todo_app_member_id from authenticated user context and deleted_at IS NOT NULL. Apply pagination using page and limit parameters from request body. Sort results by deleted_at descending to show most recently deleted first. Return paginated response with items array containing ITodoAppTodo.ISummary objects and total count. Authorization middleware must validate that authenticated user owns all returned todos.

operations.description:
Restore a soft-deleted todo from trash back to the active todo list.

This operation recovers a previously deleted todo by removing its deletion timestamp, returning it to normal visibility in the user's todo list with all attributes intact including completion status, dates, and description.

**Access Control**

Only the todo owner can restore their own deleted todos. The system validates that the authenticated member matches the todo's owner before allowing restoration. Attempting to restore another user's todo or a non-existent todo results in an authorization or not found error.

**Business Behavior**

When restored, the todo reappears in the normal todo list immediately. The completion status, start date, due date, and all other attributes remain exactly as they were when deleted. The updated_at timestamp is refreshed to reflect the restoration time.
operations.name: restore
operations.specification:
1. Extract todoId from path parameter (UUID format)
2. Verify authentication - reject if no valid session
3. Query todo_app_todos WHERE id = todoId AND todo_app_member_id = authenticated_member_id
4. If not found, return 404 Not Found
5. Check deleted_at is NOT null - if null, return 400 Bad Request (todo not deleted)
6. Update deleted_at to NULL and updated_at to current timestamp
7. Return the restored todo entity with all fields

**Edge Cases**
- Todo does not exist: 404 Not Found
- Todo belongs to another user: 403 Forbidden
- Todo is not deleted (deleted_at is null): 400 Bad Request with message indicating todo is already active
- Database constraint violation: 500 Internal Server Error

responseBody.description: The restored todo entity with all attributes including title, description, dates, and completion status. The deleted_at field will be null indicating the todo is now active.

operations.description:
Permanently delete a todo from trash, removing it and all associated edit history from the system.

This operation performs permanent deletion of a soft-deleted todo. Unlike soft deletion which moves todos to trash, this operation completely removes the todo record and all associated snapshots from the database. This action cannot be undone.

**Access Control**

Only the todo owner can permanently delete their own todos from trash. The authenticated user must match the todo's owner. The todo must exist and be in trash status (deleted_at is set).

**Cascade Deletion**

When a todo is permanently deleted, all associated edit history snapshots are also permanently removed from the database through cascade deletion.

**Error Conditions**

Returns 404 if the todo does not exist, is not in trash status, or belongs to another user.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Validate authenticated member identity from session token
2. Query todo_app_todos by id and todo_app_member_id (authenticated user)
3. Verify todo exists AND deleted_at is not null (in trash status)
4. If todo not found or not in trash or belongs to different user, return 404
5. Delete the todo record (this cascades to delete associated snapshots from todo_app_snapshots)
6. Return 204 No Content on success

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo to permanently delete from trash (scoped to authenticated user)
parameters.name: todoId

prerequisites.description: Todo must be created before it can be soft-deleted to trash and subsequently permanently erased

operations.description:
Retrieve the edit history snapshots for a specific todo task.

This endpoint returns all recorded snapshots (edit history entries) for the specified todo, sorted from most recent to oldest. Each snapshot captures the complete state of the todo at the time it was edited, including title, description, dates, and completion status.

Authentication and Ownership

The authenticated user must own the todo being queried. Access to other users' todos and their snapshots is strictly prohibited. The system enforces data isolation at all times.

Pagination and Filtering

Snapshots are returned with cursor-based pagination for efficient browsing of long edit histories. Optional filters allow narrowing results by date range.

Snapshot Content

Each snapshot represents a point-in-time capture of the todo's state. When a user edits any field of a todo, a new snapshot is automatically created. This enables users to review the complete evolution of their tasks over time.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query the todo_app_snapshots table filtered by todo_app_todos_id matching the path parameter. Verify ownership by joining with todo_app_todos and matching todo_app_member_id against the authenticated user's ID. Apply pagination using cursor-based approach with created_at as the sort key. Sort snapshots by created_at descending (most recent first). Support optional date range filtering on created_at. Return snapshot summaries excluding unnecessary fields for list display. Enforce authorization at query level to prevent cross-user data access. Handle case where no snapshots exist (empty result set). Cascade delete behavior: when todo is permanently deleted, all snapshots are automatically removed by database foreign key constraint.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of snapshot summaries ordered from most recent to oldest, capturing the complete edit history of the todo.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo task (UUID format).
parameters.name: todoId

requestBody.description: Search criteria including pagination parameters and optional date range filters for snapshot retrieval.

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific edit history snapshot for a todo.

This endpoint returns the complete state of a todo at a specific point in time when it was edited. Each snapshot captures the title, description, dates, and completion status as they existed at the moment of the edit.

**Ownership Verification**

The system verifies that the authenticated member owns both the todo and the requested snapshot. Access to snapshots belonging to other users is denied.

**Snapshot Details**

The response includes all fields from the snapshot record: title, description, start date, due date, completion status, and the timestamp when the snapshot was created.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
1. Extract todoId and snapshotId from path parameters (both UUID format).
2. Query todo_app_snapshots table WHERE id = snapshotId.
3. Verify snapshot.todo_app_todos_id matches the provided todoId. Return 404 if mismatch.
4. Join with todo_app_todos to verify todo.todo_app_member_id matches authenticated member ID.
5. Return 404 if todo does not exist or does not belong to authenticated member.
6. Return 200 with full snapshot record including: id, todo_app_todos_id, title, description, start_date, due_date, is_completed, created_at.

**Error Cases**
- 404: Snapshot not found, snapshot belongs to different todo, todo not found, todo does not belong to authenticated member
- 401: Missing or invalid authentication

**Index Usage**
Use the composite index on [todo_app_todos_id, created_at] for efficient snapshot lookups.

responseBody.description: Complete snapshot record capturing the todo's state at the time of edit, including title, description, dates, completion status, and creation timestamp.

operations.description:
Retrieve the current user's profile information.

This endpoint returns the authenticated user's profile data including their display name and account details. The user is identified from the authentication token or session, so no path parameters are required.

**Access Control**

Only the authenticated user can access their own profile. Users cannot view other users' profiles. Any attempt to access another user's data is rejected by the system.

**Response Fields**

The response includes the user's display name, email, and account timestamps (created_at, updated_at). The password_hash is never exposed in API responses.

Retrieve the current authenticated user's profile from todo_app_members table.

2. Query todo_app_members table WHERE id = authenticated_user_id AND deleted_at IS NULL
3. Return the member record excluding password_hash field

operations.description:
Toggle the completion status of a todo task between complete and incomplete.

This operation changes the completion status of an existing todo task. Users can mark tasks as complete when finished, or mark them as incomplete if they need to continue working on them. The completion status is a simple toggle between two states.

**Access Control**

Only the owner of the todo can toggle its completion status. The authenticated member must match the todo's owner. Deleted todos (in trash) cannot be toggled.

**Edit History**

Each toggle operation creates a snapshot record in the edit history, allowing users to view when the completion status was changed.
operations.name: toggle
operations.specification:
1. Validate authenticated member owns the todo by checking todo_app_member_id matches current user.
2. Verify todo exists and is not permanently deleted (deleted_at IS NULL).
3. Update is_completed field to the target value from request body.
4. Update updated_at timestamp to current time.
5. Create corresponding snapshot record in todo_app_snapshots table for edit history.
6. Return the updated todo entity.

Error cases:
- 404 if todo not found or belongs to different user
- 400 if target status is not valid boolean

responseBody.description: Updated todo entity with the new completion status and updated timestamp.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo task to toggle completion status (UUID format).
parameters.name: todoId

requestBody.description: Toggle request containing the target completion status value.

prerequisites.description: Todo must be created before its completion status can be toggled

ITodoAppSnapshot.description:
A point-in-time snapshot capturing the complete state of a todo at the moment it was edited.

Snapshots are immutable records that accumulate as users modify their todos, enabling complete edit history browsing. Each snapshot preserves the title, description, dates, and completion status exactly as they existed when the edit occurred.

**Use Cases**

- View the state of a todo at any historical point in time
- Track how a todo's content and scheduling have changed over time
- Audit edit history for compliance or personal reference

**Data Retention**

Snapshots persist until the parent todo is permanently deleted from trash, at which point all associated snapshots are cascade deleted.

Verification: snapshot.todo_app_todos_id must match path todoId, todo.todo_app_member_id must match authenticated member. Index: [todo_app_todos_id, created_at] for efficient lookups.

Password reset request containing the one-time reset token and new password with confirmation.

This request body is used when a member wants to reset their password after requesting a password reset token via email. The token serves as proof of identity, so no authentication is required.

token.description:
The verification token sent to the member's email address.

This is a cryptographically secure random string that was sent to the member's email during registration or email change workflow. The token must match a pending, unexpired, and unverified email verification record belonging to the authenticated member.

## Validation

The system validates this token against:
- Existence in the email verifications table
- Expiration status (must not be expired)
- Verification status (must not have been previously used)
- Member ownership (must belong to the authenticated member)

## Security

Tokens are single-use and expire automatically. Do not share this token with others.

ITodoAppMemberEmailVerification.IVerify.description:
Email verification token submission request for confirming email ownership.

This request body contains the verification token sent to a member's email address during registration or email change workflows. When submitted, the system validates the token against the authenticated member's pending verifications and marks the email as confirmed if valid.

## Token Validation

The submitted token must:
- Exist in the email verifications table
- Not have expired (current time before expired_at)
- Not have been previously verified (verified_at is null)
- Belong to the authenticated member's pending verifications

## Response

Upon successful validation, the verified_at timestamp is set on the verification record, making the token single-use and preventing replay attacks. The email address associated with the verification is then considered confirmed.

System-managed fields (id, email, created_at, expired_at, verified_at) and the member relation are excluded from this request DTO as they are either auto-generated or resolved from authentication context.

verified_at.description:
Timestamp when email verification was completed.

This field contains the date-time when the verification token was successfully validated and the email address was confirmed. The value is set by the server at the moment of successful verification.

## Format

ISO 8601 date-time string in UTC timezone (e.g., "2024-01-15T10:30:00.000Z").

## Behavior

- Initially null when verification record is created
- Set to current timestamp when token is successfully validated
- Once set, the verification token becomes invalid and cannot be reused

This response is returned when a verification token is successfully validated and the email address is confirmed. The verified_at timestamp indicates when the verification was completed.

The system validates the token against the following criteria:
- Token must exist in the email verifications table
- Token must not have expired (current time before expired_at)
- Token must not have been previously verified (verified_at is null)
- Token must match the authenticated member's pending verification

## Verification Outcome

Upon successful validation, the verified_at timestamp is set to the current time, making the token invalid for future use. The email address associated with the verification record is then considered confirmed.

ITodoAppTodo.IToggle.description:
Request body for toggling a todo task's completion status.

This DTO is used when a member wants to mark a todo as complete or incomplete. The completion status is a simple boolean toggle that tracks whether the task has been finished.

**Usage**

Send this request to the `/todoApp/member/todos/{todoId}/complete` endpoint with the target completion status. The system will update the todo's `is_completed` field and create an edit history snapshot.

Todos can be sorted by creation time, start date, or due date in ascending or descending order. Null date values are placed at the end of sorted results regardless of sort direction.

## Access Control

All results are automatically filtered to include only todos belonging to the authenticated member. Cross-user access is strictly prohibited.

ITodoAppMemberEmailVerification.description:
Email verification record for member registration or email change workflows.

This entity represents a pending or completed email verification token associated with a member account. It is created when a new member registers or when an existing member requests to change their email address. The token must be verified within the expiration window to complete the verification process.

## Verification Lifecycle

- Tokens are created when a member registers or requests an email change
- Tokens must be verified within their expiration window (expiredAt)
- Once verified, the verifiedAt timestamp is set and the token becomes invalid
- Expired or verified tokens cannot be reused

## Security Considerations

- Tokens are cryptographically secure random strings
- Each token is uniquely identified and linked to a specific member
- Only the authenticated member who owns the verification record can access it
- Tokens are single-use and expire automatically
